items.title: Ampleness pushes down along a finite surjective morphism in three situations
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file divisors.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The proposition says that a finite surjective morphism whose source carries an ample invertible sheaf has an ample invertible sheaf on its target, in each of three situations: the morphism is finite locally free, the target is integral normal, or the target is Noetherian of characteristic p with source its own reduction (statement lines 3892-3902). The counted proof is short: each case is reduced to one of the cited norm statements, for which a norm of the appropriate degree exists, and then to the result that the norm of an ample invertible sheaf along a morphism admitting a norm is ample (proof lines 3904-3912). It is H2: the three reductions are carried out in the counted span and the cited inputs are statements of the same chapter, two of which are cards of this lane.
